newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Metals - Aluminium premiums seen up after talks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals - Aluminium premiums seen up after talks.

text.p: Aluminium premiums for end-users in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan are tipped to rise when talks on third quarter supply contracts get underway next week, base metal traders said on Friday.

Suppliers are expected to demand that premiums for all three countries be raised to a base of US$90 a tonne CIF and they are seen to be in a strong position because of falling London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks and robust buying, especially by the U.S.
"The producers will want premiums to be at least $90 and they're in a good position to get it," a Singapore dealer said.
Aluminium premiums for second quarter contracts in Japan ranged between $80-$85 a tonne CIF.
"I think a lot of people are going to go for $90. They're going to get it because premiums now are pretty close to that level," a trader for a European metal trading company said.
Spot premiums were seen at about $90 a tonne CIF Japanese ports, and at between $90-$95 a tonne CIF for Keelung and Kaohsiung in Taiwan and at the same level for Korean ports.
"Demand in Japan is good. The consumption of aluminium by most industries looks very healthy," an aluminium dealer for a Japanese trading house said.
But Japanese end-users have said they would want lower premiums because of a slowdown in the country's economy as a recent increase in the country's sales tax began to bite.
Southeast Asian aluminium demand remains weak.
"Indonesia is quiet, Malaysia is not so good and the poor economy in Thailand has hit demand badly," a trader said.
But with aluminium consumption in other key markets worldwide remaining robust this has put pressure on premiums in northeast Asia, dealers said.
LME aluminium inventories have fallen 71,175 tonnes in the past month to 765,675 tonnes the exchange's stocks report showed on Thursday.
Strong zinc demand in Asia has reportedly prompted Chinese suppliers to have shipped several hundred tonnes of the metal to warehouses in Singapore over the past week.
"The problem is there is already a lot of metal that is off-warrant in Singapore," a zinc dealer said, adding the volume should easily reach 25,000 tonnes.
The quantity of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 11,900 tonnes on Thursday, barely changed from the previous day's 11,925 tonnes.
Traders said a few hundred tonnes of zinc were recently sold to buyers in Indonesia and Malaysia.
"They need the material and we saw spot buying from those countries," one dealer said.
Demand for copper in the region remained quiet. The surge in copper prices on the LME, where the metal touched a year high on Thursday of $2,475 a tonne, has scared away Chinese sellers.
"I've not seen the Chinese. They're not in," one said. -- Singapore newsroom, +65 870 3174
